items.title: Vacuum electromagnetic energy density and energy flux (the Poynting vector)
items.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], so
that $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a nonempty open interval, $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$
is nonempty open, $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is the position in the spatial chart,
$(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the frame basis of the spatial slice, and the spatial inner
product is the Euclidean form $\delta$; let the units and the constants $c>0$,
$\mu_0>0$ and $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be those of
[[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $k\ge1$, and let
$E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be an electric and a magnetic field of class
$C^k$ of [[def-em-fields]]. Write $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ and $|\cdot|$ for
the Euclidean inner product and norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and
$\times$ for the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]].

(a) [Energy density and flux] The **electromagnetic energy density**
$u:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ and the **energy flux density** (the **Poynting
vector**) $S:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ are defined by

$$u(x,t):=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\,\langle E(x,t),E(x,t)\rangle+\frac{1}{2\mu_0}\,\langle B(x,t),B(x,t)\rangle,\qquad S(x,t):=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\,E(x,t)\times B(x,t).$$

At fixed $t\in I$ the map $u(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is a real-valued
function on $\Omega$ and $S(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ is a spatial vector
field on $\Omega$, read in the basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$. The energy density
carries $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$ and
the energy flux density carries $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm s^{-3}$.

(b) [Regularity] If $E,B$ are of class $C^k$, then $u$ and $S$ are of class
$C^k$: they are the components of a polynomial expression in the components of
$E,B$, and the verification below exhibits the composite map. In particular $u$
and $S$ are continuous, and the definitions use no derivative of the fields.

(c) [Pointwise reading, quadratic character] The definitions use only the values
of $E$ and $B$ at the same point $(x,t)$, and they are quadratic in the fields:
for every real $\lambda$ one has $u(\lambda E,\lambda B)=\lambda^2u(E,B)$ and
$S(\lambda E,\lambda B)=\lambda^2S(E,B)$, and $u\ge0$. Consequently
decompositions of the fields do not make $u$ or $S$ additive; cross terms
generally contribute. No convention beyond the fixed laboratory frame enters
the definitions.

(d) [Products and singular support] If $E,B$ are only locally integrable (the
weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]), the products $E_iE_j$, $B_iB_j$ and
the components of $E\times B$ need not be locally integrable, and no product of
distributions is defined. The displayed formulas then define $u$ and $S$
pointwise almost everywhere, and the framework uses them only where the local
integrability of the products, respectively of the component being integrated,
is separately established. No value of $u$ or $S$ is assigned at a point of
singular source support.

(e) [Status] This item defines quantities only. The interpretation of $u$ as an
energy density and of $S$ as an energy flux density, and every balance identity
involving them, is the content of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] and of the other
balance items of this page; no identification of $(u,S)$ with components of a
covariant tensor is made here, and the relation $S=c^2g$ to the momentum density
$g$ of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]] is a consequence of those definitions,
not an identification made at this point.

references.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (cover dated Lent Term 2015, 236-page PDF)

items.physical_scope: The electromagnetic energy density and the Poynting vector of the classical vacuum framework as pointwise functions of the fixed-time fields on a named laboratory region, in SI units, with the explicit exclusions: no distributional products in the weak branch, no value at a point of singular source support, no additivity under decompositions of the fields, and no covariant identification. The item defines quantities only; the physical interpretation as an energy density and an energy flux density belongs to the energy-balance theorem of the same page, and no field equation and no empirical claim is made here.

items.title: Momentum density, Maxwell stress, momentum flux and orbital angular density in vacuum
items.statement:
Retain the fields $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of [[def-em-fields]], the
energy density $u$ and Poynting vector $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],
the laboratory region, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and its spatial
Euclidean structure of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the constants and units of
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and the partial derivatives $\partial_j$ of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Write $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ for the
position in the spatial chart, $\delta_{ij}$ for the Kronecker symbol
($\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise), $\lvert E\rvert^2=\langle E,E\rangle$
with the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and
$\times$ for the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] in the frame
basis. Let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\mu_0>0$ be the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

(a) [Momentum density] The **electromagnetic momentum density** is the map
$g:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ defined by

$$g:=\frac{S}{c^2}=\varepsilon_0\,E\times B,$$

in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; the second equality uses
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(b) [Maxwell stress tensor] The **Maxwell stress tensor** is the spatial
tensor field $\sigma$ on $\Omega\times I$ with components

$$\sigma_{ij}:=\varepsilon_0\Bigl(E_iE_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}\lvert E\rvert^2\Bigr)+\frac{1}{\mu_0}\Bigl(B_iB_j-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}\lvert B\rvert^2\Bigr),$$

in $\mathrm N\,\mathrm m^{-2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; the indices range over
$\{1,2,3\}$ and repeated symbols are not summed here, every sum being written
explicitly. The tensor is **symmetric**, $\sigma_{ij}=\sigma_{ji}$ for all
$i,j$, by inspection of the displayed expression. Its divergence is the vector
field with components
$(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i:=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j\sigma_{ij}$, the partial
derivatives being taken at fixed $t$.

(c) [Momentum flux] The **momentum flux tensor** is $\Pi:=-\sigma$, with
$(\operatorname{div}\Pi)_i:=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j\Pi_{ij}$; then
$\operatorname{div}\Pi=-\operatorname{div}\sigma$ componentwise.

(d) [Orbital angular momentum density and its flux] Relative to the origin of
the spatial chart, the **orbital angular momentum density** is
$\ell:=x\times g$, with components $\ell_i=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\epsilon_{ijk}x_jg_k$,
and its **flux tensor** is the spatial tensor field $x\times\Pi$ with
components

$$(x\times\Pi)_{i\ell}=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\epsilon_{ijk}\,x_j\,\Pi_{k\ell}.$$

Here $\epsilon_{ijk}$ is the Levi-Civita symbol, defined by
$\epsilon_{ijk}=+1$ if $(i,j,k)$ is an even permutation of $(1,2,3)$,
$\epsilon_{ijk}=-1$ if it is an odd permutation, and $\epsilon_{ijk}=0$ if two
indices coincide, in the positively oriented basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$. The object
$\ell$ carries $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-1}$ and the components
of $x\times\Pi$ carry $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm s^{-2}=\mathrm N\,\mathrm m^{-1}$.

(e) [Origin] Both $\ell$ and $x\times\Pi$ depend on the origin of the spatial
chart: under a shift $x\mapsto x+a$ of the origin by a constant $a\in\mathbb R^3$
their values become $\ell+a\times g$ and $x\times\Pi+a\times\Pi$ respectively,
so the definition fixes one origin in the laboratory frame and every statement
about $\ell$ or $x\times\Pi$ is relative to that fixed origin.

(f) [Status] This item fixes objects and index conventions only. No balance
identity and no interpretation of $\sigma$ or $\Pi$ as force or momentum flux
is asserted here; every balance identity involving these objects is the content
of the separate theorem items of this page.

(g) [Quadratic character and singular support] All five objects are quadratic
in the fields $E,B$. For a locally integrable branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] the exclusions recorded in
[[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] apply to each of them: the products
$E_iE_j$, $B_iB_j$ and the components of $E\times B$ need not be locally
integrable, no product of distributions is defined, and the displayed formulas
then define the objects pointwise almost everywhere, the framework using them
only where the local integrability of the products is separately established.
No value is assigned at a point of singular source support.

(h) [No covariant object] No four-dimensional or covariant interpretation of
$(u,S,g,\sigma)$ is defined here; in particular $g$ is not identified with the
spatial components of a covariant momentum density.
items.strategy: direct; the objects are explicit polynomial expressions in the fields and the coordinates, so regularity, symmetry, units, the origin law and quadratic homogeneity are read off from the algebra of the displayed formulas.

The item fixes objects and index and origin conventions only; it asserts no balance identity, no covariant identification, no value at a point of singular source support and no distributional product for locally integrable fields.

items.title: Local and fixed-volume electromagnetic energy balance
items.statement:
Assume the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of
[[def-em-lab-geometry]]: the fields $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ are
jointly $C^1$ of [[def-em-fields]] and satisfy, with the continuous source
fields $\rho,J$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$

pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, with $\operatorname{div}$ and
$\operatorname{curl}$ of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]
applied at fixed times and $\partial_t$ the partial derivative at fixed
position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Let $u$ and $S$ be
the energy density and Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]. Then:

(a) [Local identity] On $\Omega\times I$,

$$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E,$$

where $\operatorname{div}S$ is taken at fixed time and $J\cdot E$ is the
Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]].

(b) [Fixed-volume identity] Let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with
$\overline{\Omega'}\subseteq\Omega$ carrying the finite piecewise $C^1$
presentation of
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], let
$t_0<t_1$ with $(t_0,t_1)\subseteq I$, and let $n$ be the outward unit normal
of $\partial\Omega'$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis under which
that divergence theorem is stated. Then for every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}u(x,t)\,dx=-\int_{\Omega'}J\cdot E\,dx-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}S\cdot n\,dS,$$

the closed-surface integral being the finite face sum of that divergence
theorem and the derivative being the derivative of the one-variable function
$t\mapsto\int_{\Omega'}u(x,t)\,dx$ on $(t_0,t_1)$.

(c) [Interpretation and scope] Under clause (ii) of
[[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], $J\cdot E$ is the power density supplied to the
matter model of that coupling, so (a) and (b) read as a local, respectively
fixed-volume, energy balance of the field and that matter model. Nothing is
claimed for a prescribed current without such a matter model, for the weak
branch of the Maxwell postulate, for singular sources, or at field points
where the products defining $u$ or $S$ are not locally integrable; the
fixed-volume identity retains both the work term and the boundary flux. The
field-energy rate can vanish by cancellation of these two terms; vanishing
boundary flux alone does not eliminate exchange with matter. A conservation
claim for field plus matter additionally requires an explicit matter balance. This is a
conditional consequence of the adopted postulates, not an empirical claim.
items.strategy: direct; differentiate the quadratic energy density along time, expand the divergence of the Poynting vector by the cross-product identity, cancel the magnetic terms with the two curl equations, and integrate the local identity over an admissible fixed volume with the divergence theorem and compact-parameter differentiation.

The statement is conditional on those adopted postulates, excludes the weak branch, singular source support and non-integrable products, and asserts no conservation without the boundary term. No empirical claim is made.

items.title: Local and fixed-volume momentum balance for smooth sources
items.statement:
Assume the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and clause (ii) of
[[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$
of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]: the fields $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ are
jointly $C^1$ of [[def-em-fields]], the source fields $\rho,J$ are continuous
of [[def-em-sources]], the constants are those of [[def-em-si-conventions]],
the force density is
$f:=\rho E+J\times B$ of that clause (ii), in
$\mathrm N\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and $g,\sigma,\Pi=-\sigma$ are the momentum
density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of
[[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Then:

(a) [Local identity] On $\Omega\times I$, componentwise,

$$\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-f,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad\partial_tg+\operatorname{div}\Pi=-f,$$

that is, $\partial_tg_i-\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j\sigma_{ij}=-(\rho E_i+(J\times B)_i)$ for every $i$, with $\partial_t$ the partial derivative at fixed position and $\operatorname{div}$ taken at fixed time.

(b) [Fixed-volume identity] Let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with
$\overline{\Omega'}\subseteq\Omega$ carrying the finite piecewise $C^1$
presentation of
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], let
$t_0<t_1$ with $(t_0,t_1)\subseteq I$, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), and let $n$ be the outward unit normal. Then for
every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$ and every $i$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}g_i\,dx=\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}\sigma_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS-\int_{\Omega'}f_i\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}\Pi_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS-\int_{\Omega'}f_i\,dx,$$

the closed-surface integrals being the finite face sums of that divergence
theorem.

(c) [Scope] The identities are conditional on the two adopted postulates. The
force density $f$ is defined only for the matter model of clause (ii), so no
claim is made about a prescribed current without such a matter model. No
conservation of field-plus-matter momentum follows without explicit matter
balances and their boundary fluxes. The field-momentum rate in (b) is the
boundary traction minus the integrated matter force; these terms can cancel,
and neither may be discarded without justification. The weak branch, singular sources and
non-integrable products are excluded as in
[[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]; no self-force, radiation reaction or
magnetic-monopole coupling is included, in accordance with the exclusions of
[[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]. This is not an empirical claim.
items.strategy: direct; apply the quadratic stress identity with coefficients $\varepsilon_0$ and $\mu_0^{-1}$, substitute the four smooth Maxwell equations, identify the time derivative of the momentum density by the product rule, and integrate the resulting pointwise identity over an admissible fixed volume with the divergence theorem.

items.physical_scope: The conditional momentum balance of the classical vacuum electromagnetic field: the local identity linking the time derivative of the momentum density and the divergence of the momentum flux tensor to the adopted continuum force density, and its fixed-volume traction form with the boundary stress retained, deduced from the smooth branch of the adopted vacuum Maxwell equations and the adopted continuum coupling. The statement is conditional on those adopted postulates, excludes the weak branch, singular source support and non-integrable products, and includes no self-force, radiation reaction or monopole term. No empirical claim is made.

items.title: Orbital field angular momentum and torque balance
items.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]]: the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], the
jointly $C^1$ fields of [[def-em-fields]], continuous sources, and the force
density $f=\rho E+J\times B$. Let $g$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$, the orbital
angular momentum density $\ell=x\times g$ and its flux $x\times\Pi$ be those
of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]] relative to the origin fixed there. Then:

(a) [Local identity] On $\Omega\times I$,

$$\partial_t\ell+\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi)=-x\times f,$$

componentwise
$\partial_t\ell_i+\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j(x\times\Pi)_{ij}=-(x\times f)_i$,
where $(\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi))_i:=\sum_{j=1}^{3}\partial_j(x\times\Pi)_{ij}$
and $(x\times f)_i=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\epsilon_{ijk}x_jf_k$ with the Levi-Civita
symbol of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]], and $\partial_t$ is the partial
time derivative at fixed position
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

(b) [Fixed-volume identity] Under the domain, time-interval and
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypotheses of [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](b), and with
$n$ the outward unit normal, for every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$ and each $i$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}\ell_i\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}(x\times\Pi)_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS-\int_{\Omega'}(x\times f)_i\,dx,$$

the closed-surface integral being the finite face sum of the divergence
theorem used in that clause.

(c) [Scope] The identities depend on the origin fixed in
[[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]](e) through the explicit factor $x$; no
field-only conservation follows by dropping the boundary flux: (b) retains
both that flux and the integrated torque, which can cancel to give a zero
field-angular-momentum rate. Conservation of field-plus-matter angular
momentum requires explicit matter balances and their boundary fluxes. The hypotheses and exclusions of
[[pthm-em-momentum-balance]](c) are inherited. The density $\ell$ is orbital,
$\ell=x\times g$; no spin or intrinsic angular momentum of matter is defined
or claimed by this item. This is not an empirical claim.
items.strategy: direct; apply the angular identity of the quadratic stress lemma to the momentum balance, and integrate the result over an admissible fixed volume with compact-parameter differentiation and the same divergence theorem.

items.physical_scope: The conditional orbital angular momentum balance of the classical vacuum electromagnetic field about the fixed origin of the laboratory chart: the local identity linking the time derivative of the orbital angular momentum density and the divergence of its flux tensor to the torque density, and its fixed-volume form with the boundary angular flux retained, deduced from the momentum balance of the same framework. The density is orbital only; no spin or intrinsic angular momentum of matter is defined or claimed, and no empirical claim is made.

items.title: Closed-system energy, momentum and angular balance conditional on a matter model
items.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] and
[[pthm-em-momentum-balance]]: the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and clause (ii) of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] on
the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, jointly $C^1$ fields of
[[def-em-fields]], continuous sources, the constants of the framework, and the
field objects $u,S,g,\Pi$ of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Suppose in
addition that matter fields
$u_m:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $S_m:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$,
$g_m:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and a symmetric matrix-valued map
$\Pi_m:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ are of class $C^1$, with
$\Pi_{m,ij}=\Pi_{m,ji}$ and $(\operatorname{div}\Pi_m)_i=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_j\Pi_{m,ij}$.
Their SI units are respectively $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$,
$\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$ and
$\mathrm N\,\mathrm m^{-2}$, matching the field quantities added below.
Assume they satisfy the matter balance equations

$$\partial_tu_m+\operatorname{div}S_m=J\cdot E,\qquad\partial_tg_m+\operatorname{div}\Pi_m=f,$$

pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, where $f=\rho E+J\times B$ and $J\cdot E$ are
the coupling densities of clause (ii). Put
$u_{\mathrm{tot}}:=u+u_m$, $S_{\mathrm{tot}}:=S+S_m$,
$g_{\mathrm{tot}}:=g+g_m$, $\Pi_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\Pi+\Pi_m$ (symmetric) and
$\ell_{\mathrm{tot}}:=x\times g_{\mathrm{tot}}$. Then:

(a) [Local conservation] On $\Omega\times I$,

$$\partial_tu_{\mathrm{tot}}+\operatorname{div}S_{\mathrm{tot}}=0,\qquad\partial_tg_{\mathrm{tot}}+\operatorname{div}\Pi_{\mathrm{tot}}=0,\qquad\partial_t\ell_{\mathrm{tot}}+\operatorname{div}(x\times\Pi_{\mathrm{tot}})=0$$

componentwise in the last two identities.

(b) [Fixed-volume conservation] Let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with
$\overline{\Omega'}\subseteq\Omega$ carrying the finite piecewise $C^1$
presentation of
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]], let
$t_0<t_1$ with $(t_0,t_1)\subseteq I$, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), and let $n$ be the outward unit normal. Then for
every $t\in(t_0,t_1)$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}u_{\mathrm{tot}}\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}S_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot n\,dS,\qquad\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}g_{{\mathrm{tot}},i}\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}\Pi_{{\mathrm{tot}},ij}n_j\Bigr)dS,\qquad\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\Omega'}\ell_{{\mathrm{tot}},i}\,dx=-\oint_{\partial\Omega'}\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}(x\times\Pi_{\mathrm{tot}})_{ij}n_j\Bigr)dS,$$

the closed-surface integrals being finite face sums of that divergence
theorem. Consequently each of the three totals is constant on $(t_0,t_1)$ if
and only if the corresponding boundary flux integral vanishes for every
$t\in(t_0,t_1)$.

(c) [Scope] The matter balances are additional, explicitly stated assumptions,
not consequences of the Maxwell postulates: a prescribed current $(\rho,J)$
does not by itself supply matter fields satisfying them, and "closed system" is
a modelling choice about which boundary terms are included. The hypotheses and
exclusions of the two field theorems are inherited, and no empirical claim is
made.
items.strategy: direct; add each matter balance to the corresponding field balance to obtain the total energy and momentum identities, obtain the total angular identity by adding the field angular balance to the angular identity implied by the matter momentum balance, and integrate with the divergence theorem.

items.title: Energy flow in crossed external fields with finite-volume accounting
items.statement:
Let $k>0$ carry $\mathrm m^{-1}$, $\omega:=ck$ carry $\mathrm s^{-1}$,
and $E_0>0$ carry $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$. On $\Omega\times I=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$
define, with $\theta(x,t):=kz-\omega t$ in the frame $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of
[[def-em-lab-geometry]] and the encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]],

$$E(x,t):=E_0\cos(kz-\omega t)\,e_1=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[E_0e_1\,e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr],\qquad B(x,t):=\frac{E_0}{c}\cos(kz-\omega t)\,e_2=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\tfrac{E_0}{c}e_2\,e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr].$$

The electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to one another and to the
direction $e_3$ ("crossed" fields); $E$ oscillates along $e_1$ and $B$ along
$e_2$. Then:

(a) [Field data] $E$ and $B$ are smooth fields of [[def-em-fields]] on
$\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and they satisfy the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho=0$ and $J=0$.

(b) [Energy density and flux] With $u$ and $S$ of
[[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],

$$u(x,t)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t),\qquad S(x,t)=\varepsilon_0cE_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t)\,e_3,$$

and the local balance $\partial_tu+\partial_zS_3=0$, equivalently
$\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=0$, holds exactly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.

(c) [Finite-volume accounting] For $a<b$, $L_1,L_2>0$ and the box
$B:=(0,L_1)\times(0,L_2)\times(a,b)$ with outward normal $n$, for every $t$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_Bu\,dV=L_1L_2\bigl(S_3(a,t)-S_3(b,t)\bigr)=-\oint_{\partial B}S\cdot n\,dS:$$

Here $\int_B h\,dV$ for each continuous box integrand denotes its Riemann
integral over the closed rectangle $\overline B$; the surface integral is the
sum of the six outward-oriented Riemann patch fluxes. In particular,
the four faces with normals $\pm e_1,\pm e_2$ carry zero flux because $S$ is
parallel to $e_3$, and the upper face $z=b$ has outward flux
$L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and the lower face $z=a$ has outward flux
$-L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$. Their respective signed contributions to the field-energy
change are $-L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and $L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$.

(d) [Scope] The configuration is an ideal source-free plane wave; the
finite-volume accounting of (c) is the fixed-volume energy balance of this
declared solution in the sense of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], and the example
asserts no finite whole-space energy and no empirical realization. $E_0>0$, $k>0$ and $\omega=ck$ are the declared
parameters of the configuration.
items.strategy: direct; exhibit the fields through the complex encoding, differentiate the exponential by the chain rule, verify the four Maxwell equations and the exact energy identities by substitution, and compute the finite-box ledger with the fundamental theorem, parameter differentiation and Fubini. The real exponential derivative induction proves smoothness; the six explicit oriented rectangle fluxes use Riemann integration without the general AComega divergence theorem. A positive phase slab proves unbounded finite-box energies and hence infinite improper whole-space energy.

items.physical_scope: An ideal source-free plane-wave configuration of the classical vacuum framework on all of R^3 x R: its verification against the four smooth-branch Maxwell equations, its exact energy density and Poynting vector, the pointwise energy balance, and the finite-box energy accounting with outward face fluxes. The configuration is an exact solution of the adopted equations with no source and no empirical realization; no finite whole-space energy or empirical realization is claimed.
